subject: Intermittent gateway hop misroute & proxy surge — production impact
messages:
From: Alex Moralez <alex.moralez@stratos-retail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stratos Ops <ops@stratos-retail.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T07:22:00-08:00
Subject: High 5xx and latency spikes to /v1/generate from our prod region

Naomi —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors to the Redwood inference endpoints (us-west1) around 06:50 PST. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~5% and p95 latency moved from ~420ms to 1.4s. This is affecting live checkout personalization (many requests time out) and our throughput has dropped ~20% as retries pile up.

We rolled a firewall rule change yesterday evening to tighten outbound NATs and also deployed an internal proxy upgrade at ~02:00 this morning. Both are possibilities, but the timing aligns more with NAT/proxy behavior. We've attached request logs and a small pcap snap.

Key details:
- Affected path: requests from our app servers -> corporate proxy -> NAT -> Redwood us-west1 endpoints
- Symptoms: 504/502 on initial calls, then slow responses (800ms-1.5s) before returning 200s
- Impact windows: 06:50–07:40 PST (intermittent), continuing now at a lower rate

Can we get this escalated to SRE please? Latency & error rate are impacting revenue.

Attachments: request_logs_20261110.tar.gz, tcpdump_stratos_0812.pcap

— Alex
Alex Moralez

Stratos Retail

Subject: Re: High 5xx and latency spikes to /v1/generate from our prod region

Thanks — I’ve started initial triage. Short summary of what we see so far from the logs you sent and our edge telemetry:
- Multiple connection resets on the second hop (corporate proxy -> our NAT gateway).
- A small cluster of client IPs show SYN retransmits and TTL variance; suggests asymmetric routing for certain egress paths.
- Edge CPU/mem and token service show healthy; we are not seeing backend saturation inside Redwood.

I opened SUP-1024 to track this: https://jira.redwood/SUP-1024
Immediate next steps:
1) Can Stratos confirm the outbound egress IPs and whether their proxy pooled connection limits increased after the upgrade?
2) I’ll run a short connectivity test (curl + tracepath) from our edge to the sample IPs in your pcap.
3) If the proxy is the bottleneck, we can temporarily route Stratos traffic to a dedicated peering path (requires your approval and a quick ACL change).

Proposed bridge: 09:00 PST, I'll post a join link in SUP-1024.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: High 5xx and latency spikes to /v1/generate from our prod region

Rishi —

We pushed a firewall rollback at ~08:05 and saw a partial reduction in errors, but the latency p95 is still elevated. The proxy team confirmed they did add connection pooling improvements which increased concurrent sockets per client—that change should decrease timeouts, not increase them, but it coincides with when we started the proxy upgrade.

I attached a tcpdump snippet showing repeated FIN/ACK sequences to/from one of our app hosts where requests stall for ~600–1200ms before going through. We can join the 09:00 bridge.

— Alex
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Alex Moralez <alex.moralez@stratos-retail.com>, Stratos Ops <ops@stratos-retail.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Incident update — identified proxy connection limit on second hop; mitigation plan

Quick update from the bridge and packet analysis:
- Root cause (interim): corporate proxy connection pool is dropping state intermittently, causing a small fraction of sessions to be re-established on a slower path (asymmetric route). That re-establishment introduces the extra 600–1200ms delay and occasional 504s when requests time out at the proxy.
- Our edge is healthy; not CPU-saturated. We are seeing TCP retransmits between proxy -> NAT for a subset of client prefixes.

Immediate mitigation options we propose:
A) Temporary route clause: Stratos can add an ACL to send Redwood-bound traffic via their dedicated peering (bypass corporate proxy) — fastest fix and low-risk.
B) Short-term: we can increase our connection timeout and add a retry window server-side to reduce visible 504s (will add ~50–100ms avg latency for rerun success).
C) Longer-term: coordinate proxy pool tuning + NAT tuning to eliminate connection churn.

Request to Stratos: please confirm if option A is possible (ACL change) — we can stand up the peering route in under 30 minutes once you approve.

We will also offer a goodwill credit for the impacted window and prepare an executive one-pager; Naomi, will coordinate the customer comms.

SUP-1024: https://jira.redwood/SUP-1024
Attachments: path_analysis.png

— Rishi
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@stratos-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Alex Moralez <alex.moralez@stratos-retail.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Executive brief & goodwill credit proposal — Stratos Retail incident (SUP-1024)

Dana — following up with an executive summary and proposed next steps after yesterday’s incident that impacted Stratos Retail personalization. Recap: intermittent proxy connection churn on your corporate proxy caused an asymmetric egress path and increased p95 latency (600–1,200ms) and a spike in 5xxs during the 06:50–07:40 PST window on 2026-11-10. Our investigation (SUP-1024) found the issue occurring before our edge; recommended mitigation is a temporary ACL to route Redwood-bound traffic over your dedicated peering.

Proposed actions:
1) Implement temporary ACL to immediate dedicated peering (low risk). Rishi can assist and validate once ACL is applied.
2) Stratos proxy team to revert the pooling change that coincided with the upgrade (if you believe it’s causal) and validate connection stability.
3) Redwood will apply a short-term server-side retry and timeout increase while the peering change propagates to reduce visible 504s.
4) Redwood proposes a goodwill credit for the affected billing window; account exec (me) will draft credit amount and legal will review.

We’d like your confirmation on option (1) today; if preferred, we can coordinate a change freeze window and track the exact impact for credit calculation.
